note: Do not compare percentages without reading denominators. 'Allegation', 'study', 'court finding', 'regulation', and 'settlement' have distinct legal/evidentiary meanings. Never present a market share as the share of a household bill.

cases.name: Meatpacking & ranchers
cases.metricLabel: of steer/heifer purchases handled by 4 largest packers
cases.scope: US cattle procurement, not supermarket sales
cases.mechanism: A few buyers can possess negotiating leverage over ranchers. That does not establish how much of a retail beef price is attributable to concentration.
cases.benefits: Large packers can benefit from procurement scale and processing efficiencies; consumers may benefit if efficiencies reach shelf prices.
cases.costs: Independent ranchers can face fewer competing buyers. USDA identified recent evidence of lower cattle prices related to weaker competition.
cases.pathway: Fewer processors → weaker buyer competition → possible farmgate price pressure → uncertain retail pass-through

cases.name: Prescription drug middlemen
cases.metricLabel: of US prescriptions processed by 3 largest PBMs
cases.mechanism: PBMs decide formularies, reimbursements and pharmacy networks, often while owning affiliated specialty pharmacies. FTC found $7.3B in revenue above estimated acquisition costs on certain specialty generics in 2017–22; not a net-profit figure.
cases.benefits: Large pharmacy benefit managers and affiliated businesses may retain rebates, fees and pricing spread; group bargaining can also win discounts for some plans.
cases.costs: Patients may confront opaque prices or narrower networks; independent pharmacies and plan sponsors may have weaker bargaining positions.
cases.status: FTC descriptive findings; separate enforcement claims
cases.pathway: PBM concentration → control of drug coverage and reimbursements → prices, access and pharmacy survival

supportingSources.label: FTC 2025 follow-up: specialty generic drug markups

cases.name: Local hospital systems
cases.metricLabel: of metro inpatient hospital markets rated highly concentrated
cases.scope: 387 US metropolitan statistical areas; KFF HHI analysis
cases.mechanism: Hospital mergers may diminish local insurance-plan negotiating alternatives. Reviews link consolidation to higher prices in many settings, while quality effects are less clear.
cases.benefits: Large hospital systems may gain negotiating leverage and operating scale; mergers can sometimes preserve vulnerable facilities.
cases.costs: Insured patients, employers and independent medical practices can face higher negotiated prices or fewer choices.
cases.status: KFF observed concentration, not a liability finding
cases.pathway: Fewer independently negotiating hospitals → insurer bargaining changes → premiums and hospital prices

cases.name: Employer power over wages
cases.metricLabel: of defined metropolitan industry labor markets highly concentrated
cases.scope: BLS QCEW metro-by-industry labor markets, not 51% of workers
cases.mechanism: Where there are few local employers, a worker has fewer credible places to take their labor. BLS found a 10% increase in concentration associated with roughly 0.3% lower average pay, not a proven causal effect.
cases.benefits: Dominant employers may gain negotiating power and reduced recruitment competition; some efficiencies can support investment.
cases.costs: Workers can lose wage bargaining power, mobility and workplace-choice options; local merchants may feel reduced spending.
cases.status: BLS observational research; causal effects uncertain
cases.pathway: Few employers → fewer outside job offers → lower wage leverage → reduced household income

cases.name: Google search distribution
cases.metricLabel: of US search queries historically handled by Google
cases.scope: US general search, historically; not today's verified live share
cases.mechanism: Default contracts and distribution agreements helped preserve search dominance. A federal court found unlawful monopolization; September 2025 remedies restricted certain exclusive contracts and required some rival access.
cases.benefits: Google captures search advertising and distribution advantages; users may still value its search performance and integrated services.
cases.costs: Search competitors, advertisers, publishers and users can face fewer alternatives and reduced innovation pressure.
cases.pathway: Default placement → search traffic → advertising scale → durable entry barriers

cases.name: Digital advertising technology
cases.metricLabel: Ad exchange and publisher tools were subject to a federal monopolization ruling
cases.mechanism: A federal court found unlawful monopolization in certain ad technology markets. 2026 relief ordered interoperability and curbs on self-preferencing.
cases.benefits: Dominant platform businesses can benefit from control of multiple links in the ad transaction chain.
cases.costs: Publishers and competing ad-tech providers can face less competitive terms; effects on consumers are indirect.
cases.pathway: Control of exchange and ad server → constrained competition → publisher revenue and ad prices

cases.name: Airline route competition
cases.metricLabel: 1–8% fare increases in selected strong merger studies
cases.scope: Routes where mergers removed competitors; not all flights
cases.mechanism: GAO reported fares 1–8% higher in three strong empirical merger studies on routes losing competitors; some studies also found merger efficiencies.
cases.benefits: Airlines can benefit from network integration and economies of scale; some travelers gain more connections.
cases.costs: Travelers on routes with fewer rivals may face higher fares or reduced service quality; individual route effects vary.
cases.pathway: Route merger → fewer competing carriers → fare and service-quality changes

cases.name: Rental pricing algorithms
cases.metricLabel: DOJ litigation on RealPage information-sharing allegations
cases.scope: Named property-management firms; no verified nationwide rent effect
cases.mechanism: DOJ alleges competing landlords coordinated through shared nonpublic rental data and algorithmic recommendations. Settlements for some codefendants do not establish liability of every named party.
cases.benefits: Landlords and pricing-software operators may gain information and pricing leverage if anticompetitive coordination occurs.
cases.costs: Renters could face less independent price competition; amounts and causal impacts are not yet established nationally.
cases.status: DOJ litigation and specific consent judgments
cases.pathway: Competitor data sharing → coordinated pricing risk → tenant rent exposure (unquantified)

cases.name: Concert ticketing ecosystem
cases.scope: Live Nation/Ticketmaster; separate FTC consumer case pending
cases.mechanism: Government alleged exclusionary conduct involving ticketing and venue access. A proposed federal resolution followed; do not confuse settlement with admission of liability or final judgment.
cases.benefits: An integrated promoter-ticketing-venue company can realize coordination efficiencies and capture more fees.
cases.costs: Venues, competing promoters, performers and fans may have fewer practical choices; separate FTC deception claims are pending.
cases.status: DOJ proposed settlement; FTC separate suit pending
cases.pathway: Venue/artist ticketing access → fewer competing channels → consumer fees and choice

cases.name: Debit-payment networks
cases.metricLabel: of US debit transactions allegedly on Visa network
cases.scope: DOJ allegation in defined general-purpose debit networks
cases.mechanism: DOJ alleges Visa used contractual practices that discourage merchants and banks from using rivals. Case allegation, not a judicial finding of illegal conduct.
cases.benefits: Dominant network can capture processing fees and network-scale advantages.
cases.costs: Merchants may pay more for payment acceptance; competitive fees can be passed through indirectly to shoppers, but actual pass-through is unmeasured.
cases.pathway: Payment-network contracts → merchant fees → possible higher retail prices

cases.name: Online marketplaces
cases.metricLabel: FTC and states allege anti-competitive marketplace rules
cases.period: FTC case filed 2023; allegations pending as of Nov 2026
cases.mechanism: FTC alleges Amazon used interlocking rules affecting sellers, prices and rivals. Those claims are contested and have not been established as judicial findings here.
cases.benefits: Platform network effects can create scale advantages and shopper convenience; marketplace operator and affiliated sellers can capture fees.
cases.costs: Independent merchants may face platform dependence; buyers can face less cross-platform price competition if allegations are proven.
cases.status: FTC allegation; no merits finding recorded
cases.pathway: Marketplace dependence → seller fees/rules → potential retail prices and innovation

cases.name: Electric and gas franchises
cases.scope: Service territories and rules vary by jurisdiction
cases.mechanism: Duplicating electricity and gas networks is costly. Governments often permit exclusive service territories while overseeing allowable rates, service standards and returns.
cases.benefits: Residents can benefit from reliable network-scale delivery; utility shareholders may earn a regulated return, not a guaranteed windfall.
cases.costs: Households have limited provider choice and depend on strong regulatory oversight for affordable, reliable service.
cases.pathway: Exclusive service territory + rate regulation → household bills and reliability

critical_controls.causality: Concentration is not itself proof of illegal behavior, price gouging, or a price increase. Separate credible empirical identification from correlations.
critical_controls.comparability: Each statistic has an explicitly labeled year, geography, product market and denominator. The 51% labor indicator refers to labor markets, not workers.
critical_controls.finance: Value captured by firms must be separately evidenced; do not equate gross margin, revenue above acquisition costs, profit, and consumer overcharge.
critical_controls.ownership: Ownership and donations are relationship leads, not evidence of improper political influence.
critical_controls.geography: Do not infer a specific household's available providers or monopoly markup from a ZIP alone.
critical_controls.solutions: Separate consumer options, enforcement changes, regulation, structural remedies, and new legislation. Distinguish proposals from enacted law.

integration.question: Are rental prices affected by independent competing landlords or shared algorithmic data?
How do local hospital choices and PBM contracting affect prices and access?
Are producer and retailer markups being conflated?
How does limited local employer choice affect wages?
How does route-level competition affect fares?
Are switching costs, fees and gatekeeping documented?
Do seemingly separate brands have a common owner?
Is there documented lobbying or policy influence, rather than merely a donation?
Is there a filed antitrust class action and an actual open claims deadline?
